note: TWO CAMPAIGNS CAN BOTH MINT DECISION 0128 AND EVERY GUARD PASSES. Hit today at merge time. make preflight has a slug-collision check, but it only fires when the SAME FILENAME is added on both sides. Two DIFFERENT filenames sharing the same leading number are invisible to it, because to git they are simply two new files and the merge is clean. So origin/main minted 0128-name-the-transformation-a-quantity-is-gauge-under while this branch had 0128-the-board-gets-a-risk-scoped-lane-and-a-path-scoped-hook-rule, preflight said GO, the merge produced no conflict, and the log would have shipped with two 0128s. Worse, docs_consistency does not catch it either: its check is no_gaps_in_the_decision_log, and a duplicate is not a gap. So BOTH guards are blind to this and it is only caught by looking. The cheap detection is ls docs/decisions/ piped to grep for the leading four digits then sort then uniq -d, which prints nothing when clean. Do that after every absorption, before you trust preflight GO. Renumbering costs more than you expect: ours moved to 0129 and that meant updating five citation sites across CLAUDE.md, scripts/CLAUDE.md, two files under tools/board, and the decisions README, then regenerating docs/digest/decisions-in-force.md. Pick your number AFTER absorbing, not before.
